text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- MORE COMPANIES GOING PUBLIC IN BRAZIL
A stable currency and economy have encouraged many companies to go public over the past two years.
-- USIMINAS WILL INVEST $1.0 BLN OVER NEXT TWO YEARS
Usiminas steel firm will invest some $1.0 billion over the next two years to prepare for a growth in steel demand due to increasing auto and appliance production in Brazil.
-- BRAZIL URGED TO RAISE LIMIT ON SOVEREIGN DEBT ISSUES
Banco do Brasil President Paulo Cesar Ximenes is urging the government to ask the Senate to raise the current $5.0 billion limit on sovereign debt issuance in global capital markets.
O GLOBO
-- SAO PAULO MAYOR, WIFE GIVE CONFLICTING STORIES ON CAR

Sao Paulo Mayor Celso Pitta and his wife Nicea gave conflicting accounts over charges that a brokerage house under investigation in a multi-million dollar bond scandal paid some 2,600 reais to rent a car for her.
-- PRESIDENT CARDOSO WORRIED ABOUT EXTERNAL ACCOUNTS
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso is worried about growing deficits in the trade and current accounts and is mulling plans to promote exports.
-- ITALIAN JUDGE CONVINCED OF PC FARIAS DRUG TIES
An Italian judge is convinced that the late aide to former President Fernando Collor, PC Farias, financed drug traffickers in Europe.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- POLL SAYS 44 PCT OF PAULISTANOS THINK MAYOR GUILTY
A new poll has found that 44 percent of Sao Paulo residents think Mayor Celso Pitta is involved in a multi-million dollar state and municipal bond scam.
-- LOWER HOUSE VOTES DOWN OIL BILL CLAUSE
The Chamber of Deputies voted against an article in an oil bill that would have given distributors a five year monopoly to sell petroleum derivatives.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
((--John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414))
